knowledge_point.title: Finding the Antiderivative of a Monomial

question.:question/worked-solution:
We apply the power rule with $n=12$, and we get

$$
\int {x}^{12}\,\text{d}x=\frac{{x}^{12+1}}{12+1}+C=\frac{{x}^{13}}{13}+C.
$$

Let's check by differentiating:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{13}}{13}+C) & = \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{{x}^{13}}{13})+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(C) & = \\ \frac{1}{13}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{13})+0 & = \\ \frac{1}{13}\cdot 13{x}^{12} & = \\ {x}^{12}\,✓\end{aligned}
$$
